text:
mira: FYI I'm seeing a regression on multi-GPU runs after the proto/LL channel swap in yesterday's build. 8-GPU throughput down ~12%, all-reduce latency up on small-message paths.

sam: Can you paste the perf numbers and env? :eyes:

mira: Quick numbers from the benchmark (8xA100, seq=2048, batch=8):
```
baseline (old build)  : tokens/s = 12.4k, allreduce avg = 1.1ms, max = 1.8ms
new build (proto swap): tokens/s = 10.9k, allreduce avg = 3.6ms, max = 6.2ms
nvprof timeline shows allreduce spikes coincident with small-kernel launches
```

jon: That looks like demotion on LL channels -> falling back to a slower path for small collectives. Can you enable NCCL debug and paste logs?

mira: Pasted relevant excerpt from NCCL logs: 
```
NCCL INFO Comm 0x7f... check channels: 4 channels available
proto: trying LL128
algo: trying COLL_NET (proto LL128) -> demoted to RING on size 64
selected: RING proto=LL (fallback)
```
Seems the selection policy is picking ring for some message sizes.

ryan: Two things to try: force NCCL_ALGO and NCCL_PROTO to see if perf calms down, and run a focused microbenchmark to isolate message-size threshold where demotion happens. Also check whether our kernel selector changed IO/compute overlap incentives.

mira: Ran a probe forcing LL128/ring combos. Short runs: forcing NCCL_PROTO=LL128 gives better p99 on allreduce for 64B messages, but end-to-end throughput stalls for mixed-size workloads.

sam: Also check KV cache behavior — if adaptive prefetch touched the sharded KV layout it could increase cross-node traffic during decode, reducing overlap. Any changes to prefetch heuristics in last deploy?

mira: We did enable adaptive prefetch yesterday (runtime config flag enable_kv_adaptive_prefetch=true). I'll roll that back for a run.

perf-bot: CI flakiness alert: perf/regression/8gpu_throughput failing on nightly-2026-03-17 (job 8723). Ticket created: PERF-1234.

ryan: Suggested repro commands for folks here:
```
export NCCL_DEBUG=INFO
export NCCL_ALGO=ring       # or tree, try to compare
export NCCL_PROTO=LL128     # force LL128 fast path
export NCCL_ASYNC_ERROR_HANDLING=1
./run_bench --gpus=8 --batch=8 --seq=2048 --iters=200
```
Also capture nvprof / nsys timeline and NCCL logs. Look for periods where kernel launches wait after allreduce start (bad overlap).

jon: If overlap is poor, try reducing channels (NCCL_SOCKET_IFNAME adjustments) or increasing NCCL_MIN_NTHREADS to change chunking; small-message fallback thresholds are computed by algo/proto selector. Could be our kernel selection interacts with the message-size distribution and causes demotion.

mira: ACK. Starting a triage run now with (1) adaptive prefetch off, (2) NCCL_PROTO=LL128, (3) OLD kernel selector (rollback to commit abc123) to see which factor restores baseline. Will post logs here in ~30m.

sam: Thanks — if rollback fixes it, we should pin the runtime and do a bisect across proto/kernel changes. Also good to get a short reproducer script for perf CI.

mira: Will do. :thumbsup:
